result.topic_en: Riemann begins computing fractional derivatives of specific functions, starting with the power function x^μ: first for positive μ, then for negative μ via repeated partial integration, and finally the logarithmic case μ+m = −1.

methods.what: Fractional derivative of x^μ for μ>0 via the Riemann–Liouville integral with lower limit 0, reduced to a Beta integral by substitution t = xy
General formula for the ν-th derivative of x^μ up to a complementary function φ_ν, extended to all ν using the m-th ordinary derivative
Repeated (m-fold) partial integration to raise the exponent of t in the fractional integral for negative μ
Same power formula for negative μ when −ν > −μ, consistent with the rule that differentiation raises the order by one
Logarithmic case μ+m = −1: the integral evaluates to log x · x^{μ−ν} plus a digamma-type constant
